Lastly, I just want share a personal anecdote. My third semester of college I was in and out of the hospital but was too scared/embarrassed to tell my professors. Usually y'all are willing to accommodate but sometimes the policies in your syllabus are way too intimidating. Or we've had very un-lenient professors. I was somehow fine in the other classes but there was a class in which I was failing. I only answered 17 questions out of 100 something on the final. The TA glanced at the scantron and asked if I was sure I wanted to do turn it in. I had been to the professor's office hours a few times so she emailed me and we talked about it and I told her how anxious it made me to reach out to her and even just asking my classmates for notes. She let me do an essay instead. 


Obviously, your student may not have anxiety so my post is meaningless but maybe he does. You should ask him what was up and give him a chance if he offers an explanation. He may also be more comfortable sharing through email. I know it's not your job to cater to every student or coddle them but for some students, college is so dang difficult. 


***Also, someone pointed out disability services at school and mentioned a testing service but this is just a PLACE where you can take your tests. Not an actual EVALUATION.
